output.brief: The jump in DC-stage write-offs is most likely caused by our own night receiving, not by Haverlow. Haverlow's trailer telematics show product at 2.4–3.5°C when the doors opened, with no alarms. The chambers held temperature. Since the night team was cut from six to four on 27 July, the median time from unload to chamber has gone from 44 minutes to about 3h52. Dock staging is unrefrigerated at 15–17°C overnight. Night-shift write-off rates rose about fivefold (0.6% to 2.9%) for every supplier, Haverlow included. Day shift is flat. The warm receipt probe readings were taken after that delay, so they don't show the condition of the product on the trailer. Don't raise the chargeback or shift volume, and don't drop the night probe. Restore the night team to six, set and monitor a maximum dock-to-chamber time, and review the Phase 2 saving against the write-offs it caused. Part of the rise in customer credits may be real warm-damaged product and part may come from Corriebank's looser claim rules from 3 August. The evidence can't separate the two. Request Corriebank's claim-level data and reconcile a sample before changing credit terms. I'm fairly confident (about 80–85%) in the main finding.
